title: Remove secrets from ConfigMap via oslo.config env overrides
summary: The architecture is sound: the derived <name>-db-connection Secret is materialized with correct RFC-3986 userinfo encoding, owned by the Keystone CR (GC-managed, no finalizer), and wired into every DB-facing pod spec (Deployment, bootstrap Job, db_sync/expand/migrate/contract/schema-check, trust-flush CronJob, fernet/credential rotation CronJobs) as OS_DATABASE__CONNECTION via secretKeyRef. The ConfigMap is rendered with the 'mysql+pymysql://placeholder' sentinel and unit/envtest/chainsaw tests assert that credentials are absent. However, there is one BLOCKING runtime bug: the bootstrap Job carries an inline Python region-insert preamble that reads the DB connection directly from the ConfigMap via configparser and does not consult OS_DATABASE__CONNECTION. After CC-0080 the ConfigMap value is only the placeholder, so pymysql.connect will fail, and because the script runs under 'sh -eu' the shell aborts before keystone-manage bootstrap is exec'd. Unit tests do not catch this (they only verify env ordering); envtest does not run pods; the chainsaw test will time out on Ready=True. go vet clean, go test passes, golangci-lint shows only one pre-existing unrelated staticcheck warning in reconcile_networkpolicy_test.go.

issues_found.title: Bootstrap Python region-insert preamble reads DB DSN from the ConfigMap (now a placeholder) and will fail at runtime
issues_found.detail: buildBootstrapJob wraps the bootstrap container command in an inline Python block that does `conf.read('/etc/keystone/keystone.conf.d/*.conf')` and then `url = urlparse(conf.get('database', 'connection'))`. After CC-0080 the only value present in the [database] connection option is `mysql+pymysql://placeholder`, so urlparse yields host='placeholder', username=None, password=None, path=''. pymysql.connect will raise on DNS resolution (or auth) for 'placeholder'. Because the shell wrapper is `/bin/sh -eu -c <script>`, the non-zero exit from python3 aborts the script before the subsequent `exec keystone-manage --config-dir=/etc/keystone/keystone.conf.d/ bootstrap ...` ever runs. The BootstrapReady condition will never become True, and the chainsaw test 'keystone-configmap-no-secrets' will time out waiting for Ready=True (its 5m assert.assert budget). The Python script does NOT read os.environ['OS_DATABASE__CONNECTION'], so adding the env var alone does not rescue it. The unit test TestReconcileBootstrap_JobCreated only verifies env ordering and never executes the script; envtest does not run pod workloads; the only check that would catch this is an actual cluster run.
issues_found.suggested_fix: Two acceptable remediations: (A) preferred — remove the Python region-insert preamble entirely if `keystone-manage bootstrap --bootstrap-region-id` is sufficient (the Region row is created by keystone-manage itself, so the INSERT IGNORE may be historical dead code). (B) if the preamble is still required (e.g. legacy tests expect the extra row attributes), rewrite the Python to read `import os; raw = os.environ['OS_DATABASE__CONNECTION']` instead of `conf.get('database', 'connection')`, and keep the existing env wiring. Whichever path is chosen, add an assertion to the chainsaw test that checks `kubectl get job <name>-bootstrap -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' == 1` so this class of runtime-only regression is caught by CI.

suggested_improvements: reconcile_deployment.go:31-42 has a 'DECISION' comment asking the reviewer to verify that buildDBConnectionEnvVar returns a value (not a pointer). The value return is consistent with every other EnvVar construction in this package (all callsites use `[]corev1.EnvVar{...}`). Recommend: drop the DECISION comment and keep the value return.

integration_test.go:2154-2157 has a 'DECISION' comment asking the reviewer to verify the annotation-nudge pattern in TestIntegration_RecreateDerivedSecretWhenDeleted. The pragmatic justification (envtest watch delivery is flaky, annotation bump produces a deterministic generation change) is sound and already documented in the comment. Recommend: drop the 'Reviewer: please verify' tail and keep the rationale.

reconcile_dbconnection_secret.go:51-73 repeats the `IsNotFound -> requeue, otherwise -> requeue` pattern for username and password. The fall-through on non-IsNotFound errors silently swallows wrapped errors from secrets.GetSecretValue (e.g. a permission failure would be indistinguishable from a missing key and would just requeue forever). Consider: (1) add a comment clarifying which error kinds are intentionally flattened to requeue, or (2) explicitly type-check the known 'missing key' error so only that narrow case requeues while other errors propagate.

The derived Secret's Update path (reconcile_dbconnection_secret.go:117) compares `len(existing.Data) != 1` to force Data normalization. If a future migration adds a second key (e.g. `username`), every reconcile will trigger an Update. Consider scoping the check to 'connection value differs OR any extra keys present' via explicit map comparison once more keys become likely.

reconcile_config.go retains `resolveDatabaseHost` and `dbPort` in the same file even though the only consumer outside this file is reconcile_dbconnection_secret.go in the same package. This is fine today, but if the package is split in the future the helpers should move to a shared util. No action required now.
next_steps: Address the BLOCKING bootstrap preamble bug before merge — see issues_found[0].suggested_fix.
Drop or resolve the two 'DECISION ... Reviewer: please verify' comments in reconcile_deployment.go:31-42 and integration_test.go:2154-2157; both decisions are acceptable as-is.
Consider the minor duplication and error-flattening notes in suggested_improvements (non-blocking).
After the fix, re-run the chainsaw test 'keystone-configmap-no-secrets' in a real cluster and attach the Ready=True transition to the PR before re-review.
